questions.question: _______ is a branch of biology that studies fungi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mycology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mycology is a branch of biology that studies fungi**__.

 __
 
• Fungi are unicellular or multicellular thick-cell-walled heterotroph decomposers that eat decaying matter and form tangles of fibers.
 
• They use complex organic compounds as a source of energy and carbon, not photosynthesis.
 
• They are found in almost any habitat, but live mostly on land, primarily on soil or plant material rather than in sea or freshwater.
 
• A small number of fungi cause diseases in animals.
 
• In humans, fungal diseases include skin diseases such as athlete's foot, ringworm, and thrush.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Morphology **is the branch of biology that deals with the form of living organisms, and with relationships between their structures.
 
• **Kalology is **the branch of philosophy dealing with taste and the study of beauty in nature and art.
 
• **Virology **is the scientific discipline concerned with the study of the biology of viruses and viral diseases.

questions.question: Which cell theory proved that the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Fluid mosaic model**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the** fluid mosaic model, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of protein within the overall, lipid bilayer**.
 
• This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its **fluidity**.
 
• The fluid mosaic model was proposed by **S.J. Singer and Garth L Nicolson**.
 
• This model explains **the structure of the plasma membrane of animal cells as a mosaic of components such as phospholipids, proteins, cholesterol, and carbohydrates, **these components give a fluid character to the membranes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell Theory-**

 
 
• ** **In biology, cell theory is a **s****cientific theory first formulated in the mid-nineteenth century, that living organisms are made up of cells.**
 
• **Cells are the basic structural/organizational unit of all organisms, and all cells come from pre-existing cells.**
 
• The classical cell theory** was proposed by Theodor Schwann in 1839**. 
 
 
 
• **Model of Golgi bodies-**
 
 
• **​**In this model, the **Golgi is viewed as a set of stable compartments that work together, each compartment **has a unique collection of enzymes that work to modify protein cargo** **
 
• **The Golgi apparatus also known as the Golgi complex, Golgi body,** or simply the Golgi is an organelle found in most eukaryotic cells.
 
• It was identified in 1897 by the Italian scientist **Camillo Golgi and was named after him in 1898**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuole Theory-**
 
 
• **​**A v**acuole stores salts, minerals, pigments, and proteins **within the cell.
 
• The **solution that fills a vacuole is known as the cell sap**.
 
• The vacuole is also **filled with protons from the cytosol that helps in maintaining an acidic environment within the cell.**

questions.question: To get relief from constipation, which of the following is prescribed to be eaten in large amount?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fibre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fibre:**

 
 
• Dietary fibre, also known as roughage, is the indigestible portion of plant foods.
 
• It adds bulk to the stool, making it easier to pass through the digestive system.
 
• Fibre absorbs water, which softens the stool and prevents constipation.
 
• Consuming a high-fibre diet is a primary recommendation for relieving and preventing constipation.
 
• Good sources of fibre include fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and legumes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protein:**

 
 
• Protein is essential for building and repairing tissues.
 
• While protein is a vital nutrient, it does not directly contribute to relieving constipation.
 
• Excessive protein intake, especially without sufficient fibre, can worsen constipation.
 
• Protein is found in foods like meat, poultry, fish, eggs, and dairy.
 
• Protein is broken down into amino acids.
 
 
 
• **Meat:**
 
 
• Meat is a source of protein and iron.
 
• However, it is generally low in fibre, which can contribute to constipation.
 
• Processed meats often contain high amounts of sodium and unhealthy fats.
 
• Red meat is also known to take longer to digest.
 
• A diet high in meat and low in fibre can exacerbate constipation.
 
 
 
• **Fish:**
 
 
• Fish is a good source of protein and omega-3 fatty acids.
 
• Like meat, fish is low in fibre and does not directly relieve constipation.
 
• Omega-3 fatty acids have anti-inflammatory properties, but they do not have a significant impact on bowel movements.
 
• Fish is a lean source of protein.
 
• Some fish contain high levels of vitamin D.

questions.question: The large carnivores or the tertiary consumers exist at which level on the food chain?
questions.solution:
A food chain shows how the organisms are related with each other by the food they eat. Each level of a food chain represents a different trophic level. Animals that come of 4th level include tigers, lions etc.

__**Explanation-**__

A food chain refers to the sequence of events in an ecosystem, where one organism eats another and then is eaten by another organism. It's a straightforward way to understand the flow of energy and nutrients in a specific ecosystem. Here is a more detailed explanation:

 
• **Producers:** These are usually plants, which sit at the base of every food chain. Plants capture solar energy from the sun through the process of photosynthesis and use it to convert water and carbon dioxide into glucose (a type of sugar). Plants then use this glucose as their food/energy source for growth and reproduction. This energy gets transferred through the food chain when plants are eaten by other organisms.
 
• **Primary Consumers:** These are herbivores – animals that eat plants. Examples include rabbits, cows, and giraffes. They consume producers and get their energy from them.
 
• **Secondary Consumers**: These are carnivores (meat-eaters) and omnivores (animals that eat both animals and plants). They eat primary consumers. Examples include foxes, snakes, and humans.
 
• **Tertiary Consumers:** These are animals that eat secondary consumers. They are typically carnivorous predators. Lions and tigers, which can eat foxes or snakes, fit in this category.
 
• **Decomposers: **Finally, decomposers, like fungi and bacteria, break down all categories of dead organisms, and in the process, they return nutrients to the soil, which can be used by producers, thus cycling the nutrients back into the ecosystem.

This creates a "chain" effect – where energy moves up the levels from producer to consumer and eventually to decomposers.

questions.question: The autotrophs or the producers exist at which trophic level of the food chain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First.**__

__Explanation:__

Feeding relation in the natural surrounding:

Food chain: 

__
 
• A food chain shows the feeding relationship between different organisms in a particular environment and/or habitat.
 
• A food chain shows how energy is passed from the sun to producers, from producers to consumers, and from consumers to decomposes such as fungi.
 
• They also show how animals depend on other organisms for food.

Tropic level: 

 
• Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain that is known as their trophic level.
 
• Producers belong to the first trophic level, herbivores (primary consumer) to the second and carnivores (secondary consumer) to the third. The important point to note is that the amount of energy decreases at successive trophic levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/149da41b2e58def7608e4afb88e8bd29b90d52c1d6f0d4542f251b74e5e38052.png] 

 
• Primary producers are at first tropic level - They produce food with their own with the help of photosynthesis. Ex- plants,trees.
 
• Primary Consumers are the herbivore's animals, whose nutrition is directly based on plant products. Ex- Cow, deer, grasshoppers, small insects etc.
 
• Secondary consumers are carnivorous animals Like- small birds, wolfs etc.
 
• Tertiary Consumers are also carnivorous but they feed on secondary consumers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Only 10% of energy is transferred to higher levels from the previous one. So, the demand for food is more in higher levels. So, the food chain does not go for more than 3-4 tropic levels. This leads to more complex food forms known as a food web.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

 
• Primary (100%) → First level/ Primary (10%) → Second-level/ Secondary (1%) → Third level / Tertiary (0.1%).

• **Serous membranes;**

questions.question: What type of interaction is necessary for the survival of both the partners in association?
questions.solution:
**Symbiotic interaction** is necessary for the survival of both the partners in association. Symbiosis (also called Mutualism) is a mutual, beneficial, internal partnership between two beings. A good example of symbiosis is **lichen**, in which there is mutual well-being symbiosis between **algae and fungus**.

 
• **Amensalism **- It is a relationship between two different species of organisms, one of which is interrupted or destroyed and the other remains unaffected.
 
• **Parasitism** - It is a relationship between two species of plants or animals that benefit at the cost of each other, sometimes without killing the host organism.

 Mutualism
 Both partner benefits

 One organism (the parasite) gains, while the other (the host) suffers.

questions.question: What is the site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector)?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **"**__**Synapse**__**"**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__**

__**Synapse**__** :**

__
 
• The site of transmission of electric nerve impulses between two nerve cells (neurons) or between a neuron and a gland or muscle cell (effector). 
 
• In the **central nervous system,** a synapse is a **small gap** at the end of a neuron that allows a signal to pass from one neuron to the next.
 
• Synapses are found where nerve cells **connect** with other nerve cells.
 
• Synapses are **vital to the transmission **of worried impulses from one neuron to some other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**__Dendrite__ :**

__
 
• **Dendrites** are **projections of a neuron** (nerve cell) that receive signals (information) from other neurons.
 
• The transfer of information from one neuron to another is achieved through chemical **signals and electric impulses**, that is, electrochemical signals.
 
• The information transfer is usually received at the dendrites through chemical signals, then it travels to the cell body (soma), continues along the neuronal **axon as electric** **impulses**, and it is finally transferred onto the next neuron at the synapse, which is the place where the two neurons exchange information through chemical signals.

**Axon__ :**

__
 
• **Axon**, also called **nerve fiber,** a portion of a nerve cell (neuron) that carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.
 
• A neuron typically has one axon that connects it with other neurons or with muscle or gland cells.
 
• Some axons may be quite long, reaching, for example, from the **spinal cord down to a toe.**
 
• Most axons of vertebrates are enclosed in a myelin sheath, which increases the speed of impulse transmission; some large axons may transmit impulses at speeds up to **90 meters (300 feet) per second.**

**Myelin sheath__ :**

 
• **Myelin** is an insulating layer or sheath that forms around nerves, including those in the** brain and spinal cord.**
 
• It is made up of protein and fatty substances.
 
• This** myelin sheath **allows electrical impulses to transmit quickly and efficiently along with the nerve cells.
 
• If myelin is damaged, these impulses slow down.
 
• This can cause diseases such as **multiple sclerosis.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8576078b4f34b84fee3bd1ea63d14cd935dcaf6140e60bad1dde13b723e33bce.png]

questions.question: The structure that produces and holds sperm cells in bryophytes (non-vascular plants) and ferns is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**antheridium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antheridium:-**

 
 
• **The structure that produces and holds sperm cells in bryophytes (non-vascular plants) and ferns is called an antheridium.**
 
• It is a small, multicellular structure that typically consists of a jacket of sterile cells surrounding a cluster of sperm cells.
 
• The sperm cells, also known as antherozoids, are flagellated, meaning they have tails that allow them to swim.
 
• When the antheridium matures, the jacket ruptures, releasing the sperm cells into the surrounding water.
 
• The sperm cells then swim towards the archegonia, which are the structures that produce egg cells in bryophytes and ferns. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Megasporangia:-**

 
 
• **These are structures that produce megaspores, which are large, haploid spores that develop into female gametophytes. **
 
• Female gametophytes are the haploid phase of the plant life cycle and produce egg cells.
 
• Megasporangia are typically found on the sporophytes, which are the diploid phase of the plant life cycle and produce spores.
 
 
 
• **Archegonia:-**
 
 
• These are structures that produce egg cells.
 
• **They are also found on the gametophytes. Archegonia are typically flask-shaped and have a neck, a venter, and an egg cell. **
 
• When a sperm cell swims down the neck of an archegonium and fertilizes the egg cell, a zygote is formed. The zygote develops into a sporophyte.
 
 
 
• **Protonema:-**
 
 
• It is the first stage of the life cycle of a non-vascular plant.
 
• **It is a filamentous, thread-like structure that develops from a germinating spore. **
 
• The protonema is responsible for anchorage and absorption of water and nutrients. It also produces buds that develop into gametophytes.
